Headings, the Outline, and Page Setup

Give a long document real structure with paragraph styles, move around it with tabs and outlines, add a table of contents, headers, footers, page numbers, and breaks, and choose pages or pageless.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Apply Title and Heading styles from the styles box, the Format menu, or Ctrl+Alt+1 to 6
  • ✓Use the Show tabs & outlines panel to see and jump between headings
  • ✓Insert a table of contents, header, footer, and page numbers with Insert › Page elements, and a page break with Insert › Break
  • ✓Change page setup: pages or pageless, orientation, and margins

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Headings are structure, not just big text

On the job

You are finishing the Parkview tenant handbook.

The handbook is eight pages long. Every section title is just bold text, so there is no table of contents and readers scroll forever to find the parking rules. Denise wants proper headings, a table of contents, page numbers, and the company name at the top of every page before it is printed for new tenants.

Your task: Structure the handbook with styles and page elements.

  • Click the section title, open the styles box on the toolbar (it shows Normal text), and choose Heading 1. Use Heading 2 for sections inside a section.
  • Or use Format › Paragraph styles › Heading 1 › Apply 'Heading 1', or press Ctrl+Alt+1 (Ctrl+Alt+2 for Heading 2, Ctrl+Alt+0 for Normal text).
  • Use Title once, for the document's name at the top.
  • To change how every Heading 1 looks, format one heading, then choose Format › Paragraph styles › Heading 1 › Update 'Heading 1' to match.
Headings are what the outline and the table of contents read. Bold, bigger Normal text looks like a heading, but Docs does not treat it as one.

Tabs and outlines

At the top left of a document, click Show tabs & outlines. A panel opens on the left with the document's tabs and, under each tab, an outline of its headings. Click a heading to jump to it. Click Hide tabs & outlines (the arrow at the top of the panel) to close it.

  • Every document starts with one tab, Tab 1. Add tab in the panel adds another, like adding a sheet in Google Sheets. A tab is a good home for a separate part, such as an appendix of forms.
  • Tab options (the three dots next to a tab) let you rename it, choose an emoji, add a subtab, or hide its outline.
  • If you know Word: the outline works like Word's Navigation pane.

Page elements and breaks

Drag and drop: sort

Style, page element, or page setup?

Sort each request by where you would go.

Drag each card into place, or tap a card and then tap where it goes.

Paragraph style
Insert › Page elements or Break
File › Page setup
Place every card to check.

Page setup: pages or pageless

  • File › Page setup opens a box with two choices at the top: Pages and Pageless. Click OK to apply, or Set as default to use it for new documents.
  • Pages shows separate pages, like Word. On the Pages tab you set orientation (portrait or landscape), paper size, page color, and margins.
  • Pageless is one long scroll, like a web page. Images and tables stretch to fit your screen. It is good for documents people only read on screen.
  • Pageless hides headers, footers, and watermarks (they come back if you switch to Pages) and turns off features such as columns and page numbers.
  • To switch quickly, use Format › Switch to Pageless format (or Switch to Pages format).
💡 Anything that will be printed, like the handbook, belongs in Pages format. An internal how-to that people read on screen works well pageless.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Structure a document of your own, such as notes from this course.

  1. Create a document with a Title and at least three section titles, each with a sentence or two under it.
  2. Make the section titles Heading 1 (Ctrl+Alt+1). Open Show tabs & outlines and check that all three appear.
  3. Insert a table of contents at the top: Insert › Page elements › Table of contents.
  4. Add a header with your name and page numbers: Insert › Page elements.
  5. Insert a page break before the last section (Ctrl+Enter). Open File › Page setup and note whether the document is Pages or Pageless.
Deliverable: Submit a PDF of the document (File › Download › PDF Document) to your instructor or course folder. No Google account? Complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
